sections.title: The past participle of regular verbs
Pronominal verbs in the passé composé and dual auxiliary verbs

grammar_rules.title: Formation of regular past participles
grammar_rules.explanation:
Regular verbs form the past participle by changing the infinitive ending:
- parler -> parlé
- finir -> fini
- vendre -> vendu

grammar_rules.title: Formation of the passé composé with avoir
grammar_rules.summary: Present of avoir + past participle. Most verbs use avoir as auxiliary.
grammar_rules.explanation: The vast majority of French verbs use avoir: 'J'ai parlé', 'Tu as fini', 'Nous avons vendu'. In standard word order, the past participle does NOT agree with the subject.

steps: Add past participle of action verb

usage_conditions: Completed specific past actions and events
notes: Adverbs like bien, mal, beaucoup, déjà, trop, vite usually sit between avoir and the past participle: 'J'ai bien mangé'.

common_mistakes.explanation: No agreement with subject when conjugated with avoir.

grammar_rules.title: Agreement of past participle with preceding direct object (P.D.O.)
grammar_rules.summary: When a direct object precedes the verb with avoir, the past participle agrees in gender and number with that direct object.
grammar_rules.explanation:
If the direct object pronoun (le, la, les), relative pronoun (que), or noun in a question with quel/combien precedes avoir, the past participle agrees:
- 'Les fleurs que j'ai achetées' (fem. pl.)
- 'Ces lettres? Je les ai écrites' (fem. pl.)
usage_conditions: Direct object pronoun / que / quel preceding avoir
exceptions: No agreement with indirect object pronouns (lui, leur) or with 'en'.

common_mistakes.explanation: Leur is an indirect object; no agreement.

grammar_rules.title: Verbs conjugated with être in the passé composé (DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP)
grammar_rules.summary: Intransitive movement and state-change verbs take être; the past participle ALWAYS agrees with the subject.
grammar_rules.explanation:
Key verbs taking être:
Devenir, Revenir, Monter, Rester, Sortir, Venir, Aller, Naître, Descendre, Entrer, Rentrer, Tomber, Retourner, Arriver, Mourir, Partir.
The past participle agrees with the subject in gender and number: 'Elle est allée', 'Ils sont partis'.
usage_conditions: Specific intransitive movement and change of state verbs
notes: Pronominal verbs also always use être as auxiliary.

common_mistakes.explanation: Participle must agree in gender and number with subject when conjugated with être.

grammar_rules.title: Verbs conjugated with both avoir and être depending on direct object
grammar_rules.summary: Six verbs (monter, descendre, sortir, rentrer, passer, retourner) take avoir when followed by a direct object, but être when used intransitively.
grammar_rules.explanation:
- Intransitive (movement) -> être: 'Elle est sortie' (She went out).
- Transitive (direct object) -> avoir: 'Elle a sorti la poubelle' (She took out the trash).
- 'Je suis passé chez toi' (I stopped by) vs 'J'ai passé un examen' (I took an exam / spent time).
usage_conditions: Transitive vs intransitive usage of movement verbs

common_mistakes.explanation: Use avoir when a direct object follows.

Tu (assister) à la pièce de théâtre. Remember that the past participle of regular -ir and -re verbs is formed by dropping the infinitive endings -ir and -re and adding the appropriate ending -i or -u. finir to finish fini finished choisir to choose choisi chosen vendre to sell vendu sold perdre to lose perdu lost In the passé composé of verbs conjugated with avoir, the past participle agrees with the direct object of the verb, but only in sentences where the direct object noun or pronoun precedes the verb. For example: Il a pris la bonne décision. He made the right decision. Il l'a prise. He made it. Elle a compris ses erreurs. She understood her mistakes. Elle les a comprises. She understood them.
